correctness.rationale: For Im z>0, θ(t)=arg(z+t) is continuous and strictly decreasing, and (z+t)^(-2) has argument spread 2[θ(a)-θ(b)]. The signed inner product Re[(z+a) conjugate(z+b)] = (x+a)(x+b)+y² = |z+(a+b)/2|²-(b-a)²/4. Outside the diameter disk this is positive, so θ(a)-θ(b)<π/2 and the squared inverse kernels all lie in a common open half-plane after rotation: positive μ cannot cancel. Real z off [-b,-a] gives positive kernels and lower Im follows by conjugation. For any nonreal z in disk, θ(a)-θ(b)>=π/2; by IVT there exists t*∈[a,b] with θ(a)-θ(t*)=π/2. Setting masses |z+a|² at a and |z+t*|² at t* produces two unit kernel phases differing by π and exact cancellation. Verified both boundary z=(-1+i)/2 for δ0+δ1 and interior z=-1/2+i/4 for 4δ0+δ_(5/8) using fresh exact algebra. No finite sample is a substitute for the angular proof.
